title: Soft guardrails for microbatch admission: graded thresholds and KV-lease coordination
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a graded, low‑latency friendly admission layer that applies soft guardrails to microbatch formation under sustained high QPS. Coordinate microbatch thresholds with KV cache leasing so the runtime can temporarily accept slightly larger batches when KV hits are high (amortizing KV lookup cost), and conversely shrink microbatches preemptively when GPU memory headroom is low. The goal is to reduce tail latency spikes at 99th/99.9th while keeping throughput and token efficiency near current baseline.
background: Current admission controller flips between two extremes: aggressive batching for throughput or strict small batches for latency. Under high QPS and variable KV cache hit rates this causes oscillation in GPU memory usage and KV reservoir pressure. Existing tickets addressed hysteresis and soft backpressure (see related ENGs), but we still see transient SLO violations during KV cache saturation and sudden QPS bursts. Operators want smoother degradation with measurable cost impact and predictable tail latency behavior.
proposal: Implement a soft-guardrail admission policy composed of: 1) a graded threshold ladder (tiny, small, medium, opportunistic) per instance keyed by recent p95 latency and KV hit fraction; 2) a short-lived KV-lease signal that allows a worker to borrow additional KV cache capacity for opportunistic batches (timeboxed, non-blocking); 3) a GPU headroom estimator that enforces conservative shrinkage when available memory crosses soft thresholds; 4) an admission smoothing window (exponential dampening) to avoid oscillation. Admission decisions should be explainable in logs and emitted as metrics for Console.
design_notes: Threshold ladder defined as absolute token limits and preferred microbatch sizes (e.g., tiny=1-4, small=5-12, medium=13-32, opportunistic=33-64). Values tuned per model family.

KV-lease concept: worker can request a lease for extra cache budget. Lease contains (tokens, ttl, priority). If granted, worker may form an opportunistic batch up to the lease token limit. Leases are soft and revocable.

GPU headroom estimator uses moving-average of resident GPU allocation + predicted per-token growth from recent sequences. Headroom tiers: green (>20% free), yellow (10-20%), red (<10%). In yellow+red trigger progressive batch shrinkage.
Admission smoothing: apply PI controller with small integral term to remove steady bias; cap correction to avoid >20% step changes per 500ms.
Telemetry: emit admision.decisions, kv.lease.grants, gpu.headroom.tier as tags/dimensions. Add per-request admission_reason header for debug.
Compatibility: fall back to current admission path if lease coordinator is unavailable. Leases should not change correctness (no cross-request dependencies).
implementation_plan: Week 1: Implement threshold ladder and apply per-worker state; add config flags to model catalog to set ladder defaults.
Week 2: Prototype KV-lease coordinator (in-memory leader on node manager) and worker-side lease request/expiry handling.
Week 3: Add GPU headroom estimator library and integrate shrink path into admission flow.
Week 4: Add smoothing controller and safe fallback code paths. Start internal rollout behind runtime feature flag.
Week 5: Run canary on low-traffic region, collect telemetry and tune thresholds; iterate before wide rollout.
testing_plan: Unit tests for ladder transitions and PI controller stability under synthetic input sequences.
Integration test: synthetic QPS ramp with configurable KV hit rate simulator to validate lease grant/revoke behavior.
Load test: 1M requests/hour sustained with burst patterns in staging cluster measuring p50/p95/p99 and GPU resident memory.
Chaos test: kill lease coordinator and ensure safe fallback and no request correctness regressions.
A/B: compare baseline admission vs soft-guardrails on same workload for token cost and tail latency over 72 hours.
rollout_plan: Deploy code behind feature flag in runtime-1.25 image.
Canary rollout to 5% of capacity in us-west region for 48 hours; monitor p99, kv.hit_fraction, gpu.headroom.
metrics: token cost per request and overall throughput (tokens/sec)
risks: Lease choreography could add global contention if coordinator becomes bottleneck; mitigate by sharded coordinators and local fast-paths.
Overly aggressive opportunistic batches could cause OOMs on long sequences; mitigated by conservative caps and TTL on leases.
Complexity may increase debugging surface; mitigate with strong per-request admission reason headers and Console traces.
open_questions: Should KV lease priority be per-tenant or per-model? (tenant-level preferred for isolation)
What default ladder sizes make sense for Llama-style models vs encoder-decoder models?
Do we need persistent accounting for leases across node restarts? (current plan: ephemeral, with short TTL)
How to expose controls to Dedicated customers who want stricter headroom guarantees?
acceptance_criteria: No regressions in correctness or functional API behavior when feature flag is off.
Canary shows >=10% reduction in p99 tail latency for at least two distinct high-QPS KV-stress scenarios, with <=2% increase in token cost.
Telemetry shows stable lease grant/revoke rates and no coordinator saturation under canary load.
Feature flag has a documented rollback plan and operator runbook.
comments: 2026-02-23 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff discussion with runtime and infra teams. Agreed to prototype KV-lease as ephemeral, TTL-bound grants. Liam volunteered to lead implementation.

2026-03-01 - Liam Chen: Initial threshold ladder landed in personal branch. Observed improved p95 but opportunistic batches sometimes hit gpu resident peaks in synthetic tests. Need headroom estimator.
2026-03-05 - Priya Rao (SRE): Suggested adding per-node conservative cap to prevent cluster-level oscillation. Proposed node-level max opportunistic tokens = 5% of free memory as quick safeguard.
2026-03-09 - Liam Chen: Prototype KV-lease coordinator merged to runtime/feature/guardrails. Added feature flag runtime.admission.soft_guardrails. Starting internal canary tomorrow.
2026-03-10 - Carlos Vega (PM): Updated acceptance criteria to require <=2% token cost delta. Confirmed customer_impact rated medium and prioritized for runtime-1.25 release.
